subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up
snippet: Recap from today’s discovery + next steps for SDK auth, routing, and autoscaling sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme.ai>, Lori Zhang <lori@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Hi Samir / Lori —

Thanks again for the sync today — great conversation. Quick recap + next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Integration & auth
- SDKs: you’ll start with the Python SDK for server-side calls; frontend will use our short-lived token flow.
- Auth: propose using your org KMS-backed service account to rotate the Dedicated service key. We’ll provide a sample rotation script.

2) Routing & fallbacks
- Primary routing: us-west region (Dedicated pool).
- Fallback: Hosted variant pinned to the same model family for burst protection.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- We recommend starting with function/tool-calling in dev to validate formats; we’ll provide a JSON schema for your action payloads.

4) Embeddings / rerankers
- Suggest a hybrid approach: sparse DB for retrieval + Redwood embeddings for semantic recall. We’ll size embeddings throughput separately.

5) Autoscaling & throughput sizing
- Baseline: 4 dedicated GPUs for initial PoC (estimate ~500 qps total for short 256-context requests).
- Concurrency limits: set concurrency_per_gpu to 8 — we’ll verify with load tests.
- Queueing: prefer a request queue with 200 max inflight; use priority lanes for latency-sensitive routes.

Next steps / owners: 
- Aditya: I’ve asked you to share the autoscaling playbook + sample scaling policies (ETA Mon).
- Dev: can you confirm the auth rotation script and example KMS integration?
- Samir / Lori: please share your expected qps distribution and any compliance constraints (data residency / retention).

Attachments: I’ve attached the autoscaling playbook and a blank integration checklist to capture config decisions.

If that all looks right I’ll schedule a short follow-up (30m) next week for sizing and a joint runbook review.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

- QPS profile: our initial PoC traffic will be ~200 qps average, with 800 qps peak during batch runs. Most requests are short (<= 256 tokens).
- Compliance: we need logs retained for 1 year and encryption-at-rest with our KMS key.
- Routing: us-west works. For DR we’d want eu-west as a cold standby.

We’ll pull together the qps distribution by route and share by EOD Monday.

One technical question: for the short-lived token flow you mentioned for frontend usage, do you have example code for the exchange + minimal refresh? Also curious if the SDK supports automatic retry with backoff for the priority lanes.

Best,
Samir
CTO | Acme.ai
samir@acme.ai

Samir —

Great — thanks for the qps breakdown notes. To your questions: 

- Short-lived token flow: we have sample code in our SDKs. I’m linking the gist and attaching a minimal example for your frontend (exchange + refresh). The flow uses a short-lived infra token minted by your backend which calls Redwood’s token exchange endpoint; the frontend redeems the ephemeral token and never sees long-lived credentials.

- SDK retries: yes — the Python/Go SDKs include configurable retry/backoff policies. For priority lanes we recommend jittered exponential backoff and a separate circuit-breaker threshold so high-priority requests don’t get starved by retries.

Attachments in this message: exchange_example.py and priority_lanes_config.yaml (see the playbook for defaults).

I’ve added a proposed agenda for the follow-up call (30m):
- 10m: confirm qps by route + retention/KMS details (Samir)
- 10m: review autoscaling policy and concurrency limits (Aditya)
- 10m: SDK auth flow + priority lane behavior (Dev)

Propose Wed 30 Mar 11:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & throughput sizing follow-up (internal)

FYI — I reviewed Marissa’s playbook and sketched an initial autoscaling policy we can propose. Key notes: 

- Policy: scale-up when 95th-percentile GPU utilization > 75% for 90s; scale-down after idle at < 30% for 5m.
- Min instances: 2; Max instances: 12 for initial commitment.
- Concurrency tuning: per-gpu concurrency 8 for generation models; for embeddings set to 16 (smaller memory footprint).
- Queue config: two lanes (priority + standard). Priority max queue length 100; standard 500.

I’ll draft the YAML for the playbook and push to the shared Drive. Can we confirm the DR requirement for eu-west with Sales? If Acme needs cold standby, we should include cross-region failover notes.

-Aditya
